description: Example connector showing outbound HTTP with a stored API key injected by the host.

inputs.description: Base URL of the API, e.g. https://api.example.com.
inputs.name: api_base
inputs.title: API base URL

inputs.description: Stored by the host and injected as the X-Api-Key header; the connector never sees it.
inputs.name: api_key
inputs.title: API key

instructions: Copy this folder to start a connector that calls an HTTP API with a stored API key. Put the key in the api_key input and the service origin in the HTTP allowlist. The host injects the key as the X-Api-Key header after the request leaves the connector; the code builds the request and parses the response. Keep tools outcome-oriented: one tool per user goal, not one per endpoint.
name: example-http
title: Example: HTTP

tools.description: Ask the API for a status code and return its response.
tools.name: getStatus
tools.title: Get status
